outcome: Malicious behaviour is blocked at the point of execution, and a compromised machine can be contained without a site visit.
overview: Manufacturing endpoints are awkward: engineering workstations that cannot be rebooted mid-shift, terminals attached to production lines, and laptops that leave the site. Traditional antivirus stops what it recognises and leaves everything else to be found later. FortiEDR watches process behaviour and can block an action at execution rather than after it, which matters most on machines that cannot simply be taken offline for investigation, and the hard part is not the sensor: it is agreeing in advance who is allowed to isolate a machine attached to a production line, and at what hour.

benefits.text: Malicious behaviour can be blocked at execution rather than identified afterwards
benefits.limits: Behavioural blocking carries a false-positive cost that lands on a production machine; the rollout ring design exists because of that, not despite it

benefits.text: A compromised endpoint can be contained without physically visiting the plant
benefits.limits: Only where isolation is authorised in advance; on production machines that authority is a business decision, and an unauthorised isolation is an outage

benefits.text: Endpoint activity is recorded, so an incident can be scoped rather than guessed at
benefits.limits: Recording depth is bounded by the retention purchased; a long investigation may reach past the window

residency: Management can be deployed on-premises where telemetry must stay in-country, or consumed as a hosted service where it need not; the choice is explicit in the design

notFor.situation: An estate already running another endpoint detection sensor in blocking mode
notFor.why: Two behavioural sensors on one endpoint contend, and diagnosing which caused a stall costs more than either saves

notFor.situation: Production terminals whose vendor forbids any additional agent
notFor.why: Vendor support conditions on production equipment outrank a security preference

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to blocking on office classes; production classes follow their own sign-off
Support model: Vendor support for the platform; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed detection with an agreed response target.
1) Discovery — endpoint inventory by class, agent conflicts, vendor constraints on production machines
2) Design — machine classes, per-class policy, rollout rings and the containment authorisation rule
3) Roll out — sensors deployed ring by ring, record-only first on every class
4) Enable and hand over — blocking enabled per class against a measured false-positive period, operations handed over
deliverables: Every machine class has a stated policy and a recorded owner sign-off before blocking is enabled
A containment action can be executed and reversed within the agreed authorisation rule
Central activity retention covers the agreed investigation window, verified by a scoping exercise
